text: I'm trying to write a blurb for my image on Docker Hub that shows up in search results, but how long can it be before it gets rejected?
answer: The description can be at most 100 characters long.

gold.quote: The description can be up to 100 characters long.

text: I just created a brand new repo on Docker Hub and it has no topic labels on it. Will Docker fill these in for me automatically?
answer: No, categories are not assigned automatically to new repositories; the auto-categorization was a one-time effort for older repositories.

gold.quote:
Categories are not
assigned to new repositories automatically.

text: I start a one-off container and pass the variable by name only, with no value. My shell doesn't have that variable set, but my project's .env file has it as 1.3 and the image itself bakes in 1.5. Which value ends up inside the container?
answer: The container gets 1.3, taken from the .env file, because the shell has no value to replicate.

gold.quote: 7 |`--env VALUE`     |   -                             |   -                    |  `VALUE=1.5` |   -                     |  `VALUE=1.3`      |**`VALUE=1.3

text: My .env file sets a variable that points to a Compose file in a different folder. Will Compose also read a .env file from that other folder, and does that one win over the first?
answer: Yes, it loads a second .env file from that other directory, but with lower precedence than the first.

gold.quote:
If that file sets `COMPOSE_FILE` to a path in a different directory, Compose
> loads a second `.env` file from that directory with lower precedence.

text: I'm on a Mac and my admin has turned on both of the file sharing backends, the VirtioFS one and the gRPC FUSE one. Which one will Docker Desktop actually use?
answer: VirtioFS takes precedence when both are set to true.

gold.quote: If both VirtioFS and gRPC FUSE are set to `true`, VirtioFS takes precedence.

text: My admin turned on TCP access for the local AI model runner so other apps can reach it. Which port does it listen on if nobody picks a custom one?
answer: The default port is 12434.

gold.quote:
Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Default | `12434

text: I have a Dockerfile with a couple of FROM sections in it. If I run docker build without any extra flags, which of those sections does the resulting image come from?
answer: The last stage in the Dockerfile is built by default unless you choose another with the --target flag.

gold.quote: This means that if you don't explicitly specify a target stage using the `--target` flag in the `docker build` command, Docker will automatically build the last stage by default.

text: My Java Spring Boot Hello World image came out at 880MB because it ships the whole JDK. How small does it get in the Docker walkthrough once the app runs from a separate lighter image?
answer: The final image is about 428 MB, compared with 880 MB originally.

gold.quote: Your final image is just 428 MB, compared to the original build size of 880 MB.

text: One of the extra settings files my Compose service loads for local overrides isn't always present, and I want startup to carry on without it. From which Compose version can I mark that file as not mandatory?
answer: From Docker Compose 2.24.0, by setting `required: false` on that file's entry under `env_file`.

gold.quote: As of Docker Compose version 2.24.0, you can set your `.env` file, defined by the `env_file` attribute, to be optional by using the `required` field.

text: In my Compose file I listed a variable under a service's environment with just its name and no value, and I forgot to set it in my terminal. Will Compose tell me it's missing?
answer: No, when the variable is listed by name only, no warning is issued if it isn't set in the shell.

gold.quote: Note that in this case no warning is issued if the `DEBUG` variable in the shell environment is not set.

text: We want the cloud offload feature in Docker Desktop to be switched off by default for our developers, but still let them turn it on themselves if they need it. Which setting should we pick in Settings Management?
answer: Choose "Disabled", which is off by default and lets members turn it on (unlike "Always disabled").

gold.quote: - **Disabled**: Offload is off by default, and members can turn it on.

text: We bought the paid add-on for controlling what our developers' local sandboxes can access, but some developers say our network and filesystem rules don't seem to apply to them. Which members do those organization rules actually cover?
answer: Only members who hold an AI Governance license.

gold.quote: Organization policies govern only members who hold an AI Governance license.

text: On the usage chart for my sponsored open source images, how far back can I set the chart to look?
answer: You can choose a time interval of 3, 6, or 12 months.

gold.quote: - Select the time interval: 3, 6, or 12 months

text: My test script inside the container sometimes exits with code 1 and sometimes with 0. How does Docker Hub decide whether the automated test run passed or failed?
answer: The tests pass only if the `sut` service returns 0; any other return code counts as a failure.

gold.quote: Tests pass if the `sut` service returns `0`, and fail otherwise.

text: I've set up automated tests on my Docker Hub repo and a run just finished. How do I read the output of one specific test run?
answer: Open the repository's Timeline tab and choose the entry for that run to view its logs.

gold.quote: You can choose any timeline entry to view the logs for each test run.

text: I installed Docker Desktop only for my own Windows account without admin rights, and I can't use the Hyper-V option or switch to Windows-style containers. Why are they missing?
answer: Per-user installation doesn't install the privileged helper service com.docker.service, so features that depend on it, like the Hyper-V backend and Windows containers, aren't available.

gold.quote: Per-user installation does not install the privileged helper service `com.docker.service` automatically. As a result, features that depend on it, such as the Hyper-V backend and Windows containers, are not available.

text: Our IT team is worried that developers running Windows-based containers could end up with admin rights on their machines. Is there a way to block that when we roll out the installer?
answer: Yes, the installer supports a --no-windows-containers flag that disables the use of Windows containers.

gold.quote: For organizations who don't want their developers to run Windows containers, a `--no-windows-containers` installer flag is available to disable their use.

text: I haven't touched any resource settings on my Mac. How much of my computer's RAM will Docker Desktop's VM use by default?
answer: By default the Docker VM gets 50% of the host's memory.

gold.quote: Memory limit** | RAM allocated to the Docker VM | Mac, Linux, Windows Hyper-V | Defaults to 50% of your host's memory.

text: Docker Desktop's internal services seem to clash with an IP range on my company network. What range does it use out of the box, and can I change it?
answer: It defaults to 192.168.65.0/24, and you can set a custom subnet to avoid conflicts.

gold.quote:
Setting | Description | Platform |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| **Docker subnet** | Set a custom subnet to avoid conflicts with IPs in your environment. Docker Desktop uses a private IPv4 network for internal services, including a DNS server and HTTP proxy. Default: `192.168.65.0/24`. | All

text: I'm running Windows containers and tried to hand a password to my service through Compose's secrets feature, but it doesn't work. Why not?
answer: Compose secrets only work with Linux containers, because each secret is bind-mounted as a single file and Windows containers can only bind-mount directories.

gold.quote: Compose delivers each secret by bind-mounting a single file into the container, and Windows containers support bind-mounting directories only.

text: I gave my service a password through Compose's secrets feature. Where should my app look inside the running container to read it?
answer: The secret is mounted as a file at /run/secrets/<secret_name>.

gold.quote: Secrets are mounted as a file in `/run/secrets/<secret_name>` inside the container.

text: My containers never react to the normal shutdown signal, so every time I stop my stack it hangs before it gets killed. Can I make Compose send a different signal to one of my services?
answer: Yes, set `stop_signal` on the service to a signal the application knows how to handle, such as SIGINT.

gold.quote: - Set the `stop_signal` to a signal which the application knows how to handle:

text: I have an old project whose compose file starts with a line declaring file format 3.8. I now run it with the newer `docker compose` command (with a space) instead of the hyphenated one. Does that first line still have any effect?
answer: No, Compose v2 ignores the top-level version element in the compose file.

gold.quote: Compose v2 ignores the version top-level element in the compose.yaml file.

text: I uploaded a bunch of log files to my support ticket this afternoon and the 11th one got rejected even though each file is small. What's going on?
answer: Uploads are limited to 10 files per hour per user, so the 11th file in that hour exceeds the limit until it resets at the start of the next hour (UTC).

gold.quote:
Limit | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Maximum size per file | 50 MB |
| Uploads per hour, per user | 10 files |
| Total upload size per day, per user | 5 GiB |
| Total attachment size per case | 2 GiB

text: My teammate opened a support ticket for our company and I can see it, but I'm not the one who created it and there's no way for me to type a reply. How can I get to join the conversation?
answer: Ask the case creator to add you as a watcher, since organization members who are neither creator nor watcher can only read the case.

gold.quote:
If you are an organization member who can see a case but are not the
creator or a watcher, you can read the case but cannot comment on it.

text: On my Mac, `docker run -p 127.0.0.1:80:80` works, but `docker run -p 192.168.1.10:80:80` fails with an error. How can I make port 80 reachable from other machines on my network?
answer: In Settings > Advanced, select "Allow privileged port forwarding to external machines".

gold.quote: To expose privileged ports to other machines on your local network, go to **Settings** > **Advanced** and select **Allow privileged port forwarding to external machines**.

text: I installed Docker Desktop on a shared Mac from the command line using the option that skips the admin prompt on first launch. Can my coworkers' other user accounts on this Mac run it too?
answer: No, with that install approach Docker Desktop can only be run by the single user account specified in the --user flag.

gold.quote: The limitation of this approach is that Docker Desktop can only be run by one user-account per machine, namely the one specified in the `-–user` flag.

text: I tried to push my multi-container app to a registry with Compose, but it refuses because one of my services mounts a folder from my host machine into the container. Is that the cause?
answer: Yes, Compose can't publish a configuration in which any service uses bind mounts.

gold.quote: - With service(s) containing bind mounts

text: When I push my Compose app to a registry, the environment variables I set don't come along with it. Is there an option to include them?
answer: Yes, pass the `--with-env` option when publishing.

gold.quote: - `--with-env`: Include environment variables in the published OCI artifact.

text: I got into my Docker account using the backup code after my phone died. Is my two-step login still protecting the account now that I'm in?
answer: No, signing in with the recovery code turns 2FA off, so you need to turn it on again.

gold.quote: You're signed in and 2FA is off.

text: I misplaced the backup code for my Docker login but I can still get in with my phone. If I make a fresh one, does the old one still work?
answer: No, the new code replaces the previous code.

gold.quote: The new code replaces the previous code.

text: I turned on the extra container security setting in Docker Desktop and everything feels the same speed, except one of my containers that is doing lots of filesystem attach and detach operations seems slower. Is that expected?
answer: Yes, containers that perform many mount and umount system calls are slower because the Sysbox runtime inspects those calls for security.

gold.quote: The only exception is containers that perform many `mount` and `umount` system calls, as these are inspected by the Sysbox runtime for security.

text: My team enabled the hardened isolation feature, and I run a local Kubernetes cluster in Docker Desktop that was set up with the kubeadm option. Are those cluster containers covered by the isolation?
answer: No, Kubernetes using the kubeadm provisioner is not protected by ECI.

gold.quote: Kubernetes with `kubeadm` provisioner

text: I want to keep using VirtualBox for my old VMs on my Windows machine while also running Docker Desktop. Is that possible, and is there anything I need to turn on first?
answer: Yes, VirtualBox can run alongside Docker Desktop as long as the Windows Hypervisor Platform feature is enabled on the machine.

gold.quote: Yes, you can run VirtualBox along with Docker Desktop if you have enabled the [Windows Hypervisor Platform](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/virtualization/api/) feature on your machine.

text: I made a symbolic link from inside a running container on a folder I share with my Windows machine. It works inside the container, but when I look at the folder in Windows it doesn't show up as a symlink. Why?
answer: Symlinks created inside a container are stored as regular Windows files with special metadata (mfsymlinks), so they appear as symlinks only inside the container and not on the host.

gold.quote: Therefore the symlinks created inside a container appear as symlinks inside the container, but not on the host.

text: I ran a Docker Scout policy check on my image with no custom settings and it passed, even though I know it has a medium-severity vulnerability. Which vulnerabilities does the default check actually complain about?
answer: By default it flags only critical and high severity vulnerabilities that have a fix version available.

gold.quote:
By default, it flags critical and high
severity vulnerabilities where a fix version is available.

text: A scan says the base image of my app is stale, but I haven't touched my Dockerfile since I built it. What makes the check decide it's out of date?
answer: The tag you built from now points to a different digest than the one your image uses.

gold.quote:
Images are non-compliant if the tag you built from points to
a different digest than what you're using.

text: I'm not logged in to Docker Hub and pull images from my office network. How many pulls do I get every 6 hours, and what is that count tied to?
answer: Unauthenticated users get 100 pulls per 6 hours, counted per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 subnet.

gold.quote: Unauthenticated Users    | 100 per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 subnet

text: If I download an image that is published for several CPU types (like amd64 and arm64), does that use up just one of my allowed pulls or more?
answer: It counts as one pull for each different architecture pulled.

gold.quote:
A pull for a multi-arch image will count as one pull for each
  different architecture.

text: I installed a bunch of packages inside a running container. Does that change the image I started it from, or can I still start other containers from the original image?
answer: The changes go into a directory specific to the running container, so the original image layers stay untouched and multiple containers can run from the same image.

gold.quote: This allows the container to make filesystem changes while allowing the original image layers to remain untouched.
